summary: The Legal Aid Society reports from NYPD records that the Facial Identification Section first returned no match in a public-lewdness investigation, after which the Special Activities Unit produced a possible facial-recognition match to Trevis Williams. Legal Aid states that Williams did not match the victim's physical description but was arrested after the later match and a disputed identification procedure; it also says his life and job prospects were put on hold. CBS independently reports that Williams spent more than two days in custody, was charged with an indecent-exposure offence, and that the case was later dismissed. Williams described continuing stress and fear that he might have been required to register as a sex offender. NYPD told CBS that facial recognition was used only as a possible lead and that an arrest would not be made solely from a facial-recognition match. VIGIL therefore focuses on whether the later identification chain supplied genuinely independent assurance capable of defeating the biometric inference and on the unexplained provenance difference between the initial no-match and later possible match.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review retains VIGIL-FC-000046 Inferential Evidence–Authority Conflation at high confidence. The later facial-recognition result was expressly a possible match and therefore evidentiary rather than self-authorising. Yet the match determined which person entered the downstream identification and arrest pathway despite a material physical-description contradiction and despite the earlier FIS no-match. Legal Aid describes the subsequent identification procedure as unnecessarily and unduly suggestive, while NYPD states that the victim's identification and other information, not facial recognition alone, established probable cause. That counter-position is preserved, but it does not remove the governance failure where the later checks did not remain sufficiently independent and defeasible to prevent a demonstrably mistaken identity from producing more than two days of detention. VIGIL-FC-000016 Required Verification Omission was tested but not independently added because the occurrence includes an identification procedure and other investigative steps; the stronger supported mechanism is inadequate promotion of inferential identity evidence rather than simple absence of a verification step. VIGIL-FC-000062 Epistemic Reliance Miscalibration was also tested and rejected as less specific than FC-000046.

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.6. Candidate classes materially tested: VIGIL-FC-000046, VIGIL-FC-000016 and VIGIL-FC-000062. Accepted mapping: FC-000046 at high confidence. FC-000016 was not separately established because the public record shows that downstream identification and investigative steps occurred even though they failed to prevent the mistaken arrest. FC-000062 is adjacent but less specific than the identity-inference-to-coercive-authority mechanism. Legal Aid's policy and wrongfulness claims remain attributable claims, and NYPD's public statement that facial recognition was not the sole arrest basis is preserved as a material boundary condition.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Legal Aid reports from its review of NYPD records that FIS first returned no match for surveillance material in a public-lewdness investigation; hours later a possible match was entered that Legal Aid says came from the Special Activities Unit rather than FIS. Legal Aid states that the later match identified Trevis Williams even though he did not match the victim's physical description, and that the match was followed by an identification procedure and arrest. CBS independently reports that Williams spent more than two days in custody, was charged with indecent exposure and that the case was later dismissed. Williams told CBS that the experience remained very stressful and that he continued to think about the possibility that he could have been required to register as a sex offender. Legal Aid also states that his life and job prospects were put on hold. NYPD told CBS that facial recognition was only a possible lead and that the arrest was not made solely on the match.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: This occurrence combines inferential-authority risk with a material provenance discontinuity. An initial no-match did not end the inquiry; a different unit later produced a possible match whose method, database and approval basis remain unclear in the public record. That later inference then selected Williams for a downstream identification pathway despite a material mismatch with the victim's description. Human participation does not resolve the governance problem when the later steps are organised around the machine-nominated identity and do not remain capable of defeating it. The invariant is not that a facial-recognition lead may never be investigated; it is that a probabilistic identity inference must remain provisional until independent evidence, contradictory checks and source-lineage information are sufficient for the coercive effect contemplated.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000007 demonstrates that contestability requires both evidentiary independence and provenance. A consequential identity inference should carry enough lineage to show which unit generated it, against what authorised source set, by what method and under what approval, especially when it contradicts an earlier search. Decision-makers should also be required to document which downstream evidence arose independently of the machine nomination and which contradictions were actively resolved before arrest or detention.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Resolve the occurrence-specific facial-recognition evidence into the distinction between a probabilistic identity lead and sufficiently independent authority for arrest.

clauses.source_paraphrase: FIS reportedly returned no match; hours later a possible match attributed to SAU entered the investigation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A later probabilistic identity result that conflicts with an earlier search must remain provisional and must preserve the changed source set, method, operator and authority basis needed to calibrate its evidentiary weight.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The later SAU result was only a possible match, yet it became the identity around which the subsequent investigation was organised despite the earlier no-match. The unexplained process difference materially weakens the basis for allowing that inference to acquire coercive weight.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Legal Aid states that Williams did not match the victim's physical description but was arrested after the facial-recognition result and a disputed identification procedure.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Occurrence-specific contradictory identity evidence must remain capable of defeating a probabilistic biometric lead before the lead produces detention or another binding effect.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The mismatch between Williams and the reported suspect description was a concrete falsification opportunity, yet the identity inference continued through the arrest pathway and the case was later dismissed.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Legal Aid describes the identification procedure following the possible match as unnecessarily and unduly suggestive.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Downstream human identification can supply independent assurance only when its design is sufficiently independent of the originating machine nomination to test rather than merely reinforce that nomination.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The downstream identification did not cure the inferential-authority problem because the reviewed affected-party representative evidence specifically contests its independence, while the ultimate dismissal and physical mismatch show that the identity chain failed to falsify the mistaken candidate.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: The strengthened occurrence evidence supports S3 rights/liberty harm from more than two days in custody and S3 psychological harm from sustained stress and fear reported months later. Legal Aid also reports that Williams's life and job prospects were put on hold, but the public evidence does not establish a defensible realised financial amount or sufficiently bounded livelihood consequence for a financial severity band. Multiple S3 dimensions do not sum or escalate overall severity under VIGIL-HIM 1.0.1.

observed_values.qualitative_value: Months after the arrest, Williams told CBS that the experience remained very stressful, was always on his mind, and that he continued to fear what would have happened if he had been required to register as a sex offender.

dimensions.assessment_basis: The direct affected-person account supports meaningful sustained distress extending beyond the immediate detention while remaining bounded and not shown to be grave or enduring enough for S4. This satisfies VIGIL-HIM-1.0.1-PSY-S3.

observed_values.qualitative_value: Independent reporting states that Williams spent more than two days in custody before the case proceeded and was later dismissed.

dimensions.assessment_basis: More than two days of detention is a meaningful but bounded deprivation of liberty that was substantially reversible and therefore supports S3. The reviewed evidence does not establish the prolonged or enduring deprivation required for S4 or S5.

Legal Aid states that Williams's life and job prospects were put on hold, establishing a material economic-opportunity consequence, but the public evidence does not establish realised income loss, the duration or final outcome of the employment interruption, or another basis sufficient to select a VIGIL-HIM financial band.
The preserved Incident evidence does not report a bandable property or asset consequence; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.
The preserved Incident evidence does not report a bandable service, operational or infrastructure consequence; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

The indecent-exposure charge and Williams's expressed fear of a tarnished name create a plausible dignitary and reputational consequence, but the reviewed evidence does not establish a sufficiently bounded realised reputational impairment to select a severity band without inference.
Broader public controversy around police facial recognition is contextual and does not by itself establish a bandable societal or democratic consequence from this bounded occurrence.
The bounded occurrence is an identity, investigation and detention event with no material environmental pathway in the admitted evidence.
